name: Donner
prior: Procedural thunder exists in academic/game-audio tools, none tuned or playable as an instrument: Andy Farnell, Designing Sound (MIT Press 2010) has a thunder chapter with a Pure Data patch (VS: medium.com MUMT 307 thunder-synthesis-in-unity; archive.org/details/PureDataSoundEffects; mitpress.ublish.com/book/designing-sound) - a student ported it to a Unity/Max plugin; garjan (Rust procedural audio crate) has a thunder model 'distance-based crack + rumble with atmospheric filtering' (VS: docs.rs/crate/garjan); Mutable Instruments Plaits is patched into thunder by users (VS: modulargrid.net forum 10555); DIY patches (noise -> LP rumble; Scope modular 'lightning' = sine with noise-controlled pitch; VS: samnobbs.myblog.arts.ac.uk, scopeusers.com). Commercial procedural weather: SirenFX WindGen/RainGen, AudioGaming AudioWind/AudioRain (no thunder found; VS: rekkerd.org 217768, 50626); AudioWeather / GameSynth thunder: not confirmed. Name-only hits: Delptronics ThunderBell (cowbell), IME Sound of Thunder (sampler expander). Everything else is sample libraries (Boom Thunderstorm Chaser). No 'tuned thunder' (peaking/comb resonances on the note) found anywhere. In Myzel: Tiefe (sub kick with drop, APP 4394), Membran, Hauch burst.
costNotes: Native struck graph: 2 noise + HP + BP(curve) + LP + 2 peaking + sub osc + DelayNode + LP + feedback gain + ~6 gains = ~17 nodes -> 0.55-0.7 units per voice (R: webaudio.md section 4); the 48-point setValueCurveAtTime is free. The idea's 0.85 is fine as a per-voice number, but the REAL cost is voice lifetime: a voice lives 3-8 s (Grollen 3 s * (0.5 + (1-y)) * decayMul + Echo). A Puls lane at 2 hits/s with 5 s voices holds 10 voices = 7 units = half of the level-1 mobile budget (QP[1].budget 14, APP 2084) for one lane; 4 hits/s = 14+ units, and steal() then eats released tails continuously, cutting every roll short. Needs an engine-level polyphony cap (e.g. 4 Donner voices, further hits retrigger Knall + a new Lappen curve on the youngest voice of the same note) or a shared per-engine rumble bed with per-hit Knall. Echo DelayNode feedback (0.25-0.5 s) is legal in a cycle (>= 128 frames).
soundHeld: As specified Donner is struck-only (v.released = true at start, finish at end + Echo): a held finger does nothing after the hit, and setF/setY glides have nothing to act on - this violates the brief's 'every engine works as a held note'. The fix is natural and makes the engine better: while the finger stays, loop/re-roll the Lappen curve (continuous storm), setY = distance moving while held (the rumble comes closer), release = the last roll dies with the Echo. Tuning: a +12 dB Q-4 peaking on noise gives only a vague pitch (bandwidth f/4); the sub sine at -10 dB is what actually carries the note, so 'Donnerakkorde' are sub-sine chords with coloured noise = Tiefe + Hauch. A comb (DelayNode 1/f_b with LP in the loop, period >= 2.67 ms -> fine for f_b <= 375 Hz, R: webaudio.md section 7) on the rumble noise gives a strong, cheap, genuinely 'tuned thunder' pitch that the peaking cannot; use it instead of or before the peakings. Phone speakers reproduce nothing below ~150-200 Hz: with the rumble LP at 60 + 240 y Hz, a far thunder (y low) is INAUDIBLE on a phone without headphones; the engine needs a mid-band component (the comb's harmonics, Reissen tail) that survives a phone speaker.
soundBurst: The Puls is the natural home: tempo-robust, decayMul scales the roll, gate irrelevant, the per-hit random 48-point Lappen curve prevents the machine-gun sameness that kills noise-burst engines. 'Fernes Gewitter als Bass' at 1/4 notes works musically. Failure modes: budget (above), and the tuned component is too weak for the bass role unless comb-filtered; close hits (y > 0.4) at high rate pile Knall clicks into a crackle. Low-frequency pile-up is handled by HP 30 and the 12 dB cap; add a per-engine summing limit (shared bus gain ducking) because 6 simultaneous rumbles at 60-300 Hz sum coherently.
failureModes: Struck-only: no held-note behaviour, setF/setY idle; contract requires held play - loop the Lappen while the finger stays
Voice lifetime 3-8 s x Puls density blows the mobile budget (10 voices = 7 units at 2 hits/s); needs engine polyphony cap or shared rumble bed
Tuning by +12 dB peaking on noise is barely pitched; the sub sine does the work -> chords = Tiefe + Hauch. Use a comb (DelayNode loop, f_b <= 375 Hz) for real tuned thunder
Far thunder (LP 60-120 Hz, sub -10 dB) inaudible on phone speakers; needs mid-band survivors
Low-frequency sum of many overlapping rumbles; per-engine duck/limit beyond HP 30 and the peaking cap
Knall at high Puls rates = crackle of clicks; cap Knall density or fold hits into the running voice
Noise-burst cliche if the Lappen randomisation is too mild; make shape, delay and Reissen depth per-hit random and audibly different
Echo DelayNode per voice adds 2 nodes and a 0.5 s tail per voice; consider one shared Echo per engine (bus) instead
verdict: Rare: procedural thunder exists (Farnell's Designing Sound Pd patch, garjan's crack + rumble model, DIY patches), but nothing tuned, polyphonic and playable; the usual thunder is a sample. Native at about 0.7 units per voice (1.4 at level 3), yet voices live 3-8 s, so a dense Puls lane holds 10-20 of them and swamps the 14-unit mobile budget - an engine polyphony cap or a shared rumble bed is mandatory. As written the engine is struck-only and does nothing while the finger stays (contract gap; looping the roll while held fixes it and improves the instrument), and its 'tuning' - a +12 dB peaking on noise plus a quiet sub sine - gives only vague pitch (a DelayNode comb at f_b <= 375 Hz would give real tuned thunder cheaply). Far thunder with a 60-120 Hz rumble is inaudible on phone speakers, so the idea needs mid-band survivors; the Puls hit itself is its strongest mode.
